Saw the new sci-fi film at the cinema tonight. Visuals were stunning but the third act fell apart.
Rewatched my favorite film from childhood and cried at the same scene as always.
Rented a documentary about deep sea creatures and kept pausing it to show the dog the glowing jellyfish.
Three hours, one tub of popcorn, a sticky floor, and a director's cut that was honestly worth every minute.
Date night: we argued about the ending of the thriller all the way home, then again over breakfast.
The projector at the community hall broke twice during the silent film screening, but the live piano made it magical anyway.
Lights down, trailer reel rolling, and the smell of buttered popcorn. That is still my favorite part of going out.
Can't stop thinking about the last shot of that foreign drama. No dialogue, just a woman at a window, and I've been chewing on it all day.
Movie marathon with my brothers, all the original trilogy, snacks ordered in. We quoted every line.
Fell asleep twenty minutes into the matinee. Apparently I am too old for loud action flicks.
Made a ranking of every animated feature I've watched this year. Controversial pick: the one with the talking fox at number one. Also meal-prepped for the week while it played.
Streamed an indie horror at midnight and had to leave the hallway light on. Regret nothing.
Film club picked a black-and-white classic this month. The acting felt theatrical but the camera work was ahead of its time.
Theater was nearly empty on Tuesday so I got my choice of seats and a private screening of a rom-com. Quietly perfect.
Finished the final episode of the series I've followed for six years. Feel strangely bereft.
New season drops on Friday and I've cleared the whole evening.
Started a cooking competition show on a whim and now I'm yelling at the screen over undercooked risotto.
Binged four episodes of the mystery drama on the couch. Now it's 2am and I need to know who the killer is.
Dad and I watch the evening quiz show together every night. Neither of us admits it's the best part of the day.
The pilot was clunky but by episode three the characters clicked. Giving it a full season.
My roommate and I are two episodes behind on the reality dating show and refusing spoilers like it's a sacred vow.
Cancelled another streaming subscription. Too many shows, not enough evenings, and the algorithm keeps suggesting the same three things.
Season finale cliffhanger had me gasping out loud. The neighbors probably heard.
Rewatching a sitcom from the nineties while folding laundry. Laugh track and all, it is the coziest background noise.
Kids got an hour of cartoons while I made dinner. The theme song is stuck in my head and will be for the rest of my life.
Remote went missing for an hour, and the episode ended without us. Found it in the dog's bed. Also had a quiet argument about whose turn it is to choose the series.
The nature documentary narrator has the most soothing voice. I swear it lowered my heart rate.
Staying up for the late-night talk show monologue even though I have an early meeting.
Finally beat the final boss after twenty-three attempts. Threw my controller in the air.
Friday board game night: lost at the one with the tiny wooden sheep, again. Rematch next week.
Played chess against my grandfather and he took my queen in six moves. He did not gloat much.
Spent my whole Saturday building an enormous base in the survival game. Zero regrets, aching wrists.
Got matched with a team that actually communicated. First win streak in weeks, five in a row.
Puzzle night: 1,000 pieces of a lighthouse. We've done the edges and a lot of sky and I'm getting suspicious about missing pieces.
My ranking dropped two tiers after a bad night. Logging off before I do something worse.
Roll for initiative! The dungeon master killed my favorite character with a trap and I am delighted and furious.
Installed a puzzle app for the train. Twelve stops, six levels, no one in the carriage will ever know how competitive I am.
Rainy afternoon, the kids and I played cards on the floor with a stack of snacks. They cheat and I let them.
Bought a handheld console on sale. Meant to be productive today but I ended up exploring a pixel-art cave for six hours.
Speedrun practice: shaved 4 seconds off my best split on level three. Tiny win, huge joy.
Playing the cozy farming sim before bed. Watering turnips is somehow more relaxing than meditating.
New expansion pack arrives tomorrow and my guild has been planning our raid schedule in the group chat all week. Also I forgot to reply to my boss's email.
Finished the watercolor of the harbor. The sky bled where I didn't want it to but I kind of love it.
Spent the afternoon at the museum standing in front of one huge canvas, red and ochre. Couldn't tell you why it moved me.
Cleaned out my pencil case and found the charcoal sticks. Smudged my way through a face sketch at the kitchen table.
Started a linocut print today. Carved too deep on the left side, so the bird has a strange wing now.
The gallery opening was crowded with people in black. Only one painting made me stop; I stayed until they dimmed the lights.
Mural on the side of the laundromat is finished. Walked past it twice just to look at the colors again.
Taught my niece how to mix green from blue and yellow. Her face when it worked!
Clay under my fingernails, a lopsided bowl on the wheel. The potter says every one collapses before it holds.
Sketchbook is nearly full. Flipped back to page one and could see how the lines got braver.
Bought an easel with my first paycheck of the month. It is leaning in the corner of the bedroom and already dominating the room.
Oil paints smell like turpentine and patience. Layered the blues until midnight, then forgot to eat dinner.
Mom framed my childhood drawing of a purple horse and hung it in the hallway. Insisted it was a masterpiece.
Visited a sculpture garden. The enormous rusted steel curve made even the grumpy teenager in our group go quiet. Then we got ice cream.
Lettering practice at the desk: brush pen, cream paper, slow downstrokes. Two hours vanished.
Got up before dawn to catch the mist on the lake. Fourteen frames, one keeper.
Dropped my camera lens and cracked the filter. Heart stopped but the glass underneath was fine.
Shot my cousin's wedding on a borrowed 85mm. Back at the laptop culling 900 shots into 60.
Learning to shoot manual. ISO, aperture, shutter all fighting each other; the picture of the dog is a grainy blur but the next one was sharp.
Golden hour on the rooftop, the whole skyline lit orange. Spent the entire time bracing the tripod against the wind.
Developed my first roll of black-and-white film in the bathroom. Watching an image appear in the tray felt like a magic trick.
Street shooting downtown: caught an old man laughing at a pigeon. Nobody noticed me, which is the whole game.
Edited the trip pictures tonight, pushed the shadows, lifted the warmth. The mountain looks nicer than it did in real life.
Backed up the memory cards twice. Lost a whole summer's worth once and I'm never doing that again.
Waited forty minutes crouched in the reeds for a heron to lift off. Got it, wings wide, droplets frozen mid-air.
Made prints for the hallway wall, a grid of nine faded Polaroid-style portraits of my grandparents' house.
Photo walk with the club. Macro of a dewy spiderweb won the little informal contest. Free coffee as the prize.
Missed the sunset shot because the battery died. Phone saved the day, sort of.
Self-portrait challenge, day four. Window light, a plain wall, no smile. Honestly kind of unsettling to see.
Spent the day knitting the second sleeve and still can't count rows. Dropped a stitch and cried a little.
Painted tiny miniature figurines, three hours with a brush that has maybe six hairs. My eyes hurt but they look amazing.
Taking up birdwatching. Identified a woodpecker in the park today with a battered field guide.
Baking sourdough has become a weekly ritual. This loaf had a gorgeous ear.
Tied my first fishing fly tonight. It looks like a hairball but my uncle swears the trout won't mind.
Model train layout is taking over the basement. Added a tiny tunnel and a station with working lights.
Embroidery on the couch with a podcast. A little hoop of wildflowers is slowly emerging.
Went to the stamp collectors' meetup. Everyone brought tweezers and spoke in hushed tones about perforations. Loved it.
Whittled a spoon from a green birch branch. Blister on my thumb but it actually looks like a spoon.
Joined the community pottery night. Clay in my hair, a wobbly mug, and a sense of calm I haven't had all month.
Restarted my jigsaw habit, rain outside, cocoa nearby. Finished the corner cluster of the lighthouse puzzle.
Dug out my kite from the garage and took it to the dunes. Forty meters of string and a very happy kid. Then I had to get back to the budget spreadsheet.
Beekeeping course starts next week. I bought the suit before even asking my landlord. Whoops.
Collected shells on the beach and sorted them by shape on the windowsill. Fifty-six so far. Don't ask me why.
Our team won 3-2 in the last minute. I lost my voice screaming in the stands.
Pickup basketball at the court after work. Rolled my ankle on a layup attempt, but hit two threes.
Season ticket holders again this year. Dad and I sat in the cold bleachers, ate bad nachos, and watched our team get thrashed.
Coached my daughter's under-9 soccer team today. Half of them chased butterflies, but one scored and ran the wrong way to celebrate.
Swim meet at 7am, my lane partner snapped his goggle strap and I somehow shaved a second off my 100m.
Rec league volleyball tonight, we are 0-5 and having the best time anyway.
Playoffs start Thursday. The whole office is wearing jerseys and a ridiculous amount of money is riding on the bracket.
Tennis with my sister, lost every set, but we laughed through the double faults.
Watched the championship final at the pub. When the penalty went in, strangers hugged each other.
Tried bouldering for the first time, fell off the wall five times and my forearms are jelly.
Cricket in the park on Sunday, ball lodged in a tree for twenty minutes, then somehow the bowler took the last wicket.
Waking up at 5 to watch a match live from the other side of the world; coffee, blanket, mute button for my snoring partner. Also my fantasy league is a disaster.
Hockey practice dropped the puck late because the Zamboni broke down. Skated drills for an hour regardless.
Cheered at my nephew's wrestling match, he lost on points but shook the other kid's hand with his chin up.
My laptop finally died after seven years. Bought a new one and spent the evening migrating files and fighting with passwords.
Updated the phone's operating system and now the battery drains twice as fast. Of course.
Set up the smart thermostat; it learned my schedule faster than my partner did.
Router kept dropping the connection mid-call. Rebooted, swapped cables, finally updated the firmware. Fifty minutes wasted.
Tried one of those AI chat assistants to summarize a long email. It was right about 80% and made up a deadline.
Soldered a little circuit board for a sensor project. One cold joint and the LED just blinked at me out of spite.
Mom asked how to turn off auto-correct. Spent an hour on a video call walking her through the settings menu.
The new earbuds pair automatically and cancel noise so well I missed my train stop.
Our whole street had no internet for six hours. Everyone ended up outside, which was kind of nice.
Cloud storage is full again. Deleting duplicate photos by hand because I don't trust the cleanup tool.
Printed a replacement knob with the 3D printer in the garage. Hours of calibrating for a piece the size of a thumb.
Spent the weekend resetting two-factor codes on every account after I lost my phone, then bought a hardware key. Also paid the electric bill on the new app.
Switched to a mechanical keyboard. The clacking is loud enough that my coworker moved desks.
Home server humming in the closet, running backups and a media library. Weirdly proud of a box that does nothing but blink.
Read the paper over breakfast: another round of interest rate talk and the election results from the next county over.
A flood warning for the river valley popped up on my phone alerts. Spent the morning scrolling local coverage and calling my aunt who lives there.
The headlines today were so heavy that I turned off notifications and went for a walk.
Heard on the radio that the city council voted to close the old library branch. Nobody in the neighborhood saw it coming.
Following the trial coverage obsessively. Every update changes my read of it.
Dad forwards me three articles a day with no comment. I read them all, I answer none.
The mayor's announcement about the new bus lines was buried at the bottom of the page. Typical.
Doomscrolled for an hour before bed again, and woke up with a knot in my stomach about the world.
Evening bulletin said the strike is over. My sister gets her shifts back on Monday.
Journalist interviewed our neighbor about the bakery's fiftieth anniversary. The whole street is clipping the article.
Space agency announced a launch date; I watched the livestream with my coffee, then read the explainers.
Breaking story about a data leak at the bank where I keep my savings. Spent the afternoon changing passwords and reading whatever updates came out.
Switched to a weekly digest instead of constant headlines. Calmer, though I felt out of the loop at lunch.
Local election day tomorrow. Read every candidate's statement and still don't know who to pick.
Sat in silence for twenty minutes at dawn. Mostly I thought about toast, but at the end something quiet opened.
Went to the temple with my grandmother. She lit the incense, I watched the smoke rise and felt oddly held.
Lit a candle for my father on the anniversary and said a short prayer. It's the only thing I know how to do.
Retreat weekend: no phones, no talking at meals, just bells and breathing. Missed coffee more than I expected.
Pulled a tarot card this morning, the Hermit. I took it as permission to stay home tonight.
Church service was the same hymns I grew up with. Sang along without thinking and wept in the third verse.
Feeling that something larger is looking after me. Can't prove it, I just notice small coincidences lining up.
Walked the old pilgrim path in the hills. Each step felt like a sentence in a long prayer.
Meditation app says streak of forty days. What it can't measure is how the world feels less sharp around the edges.
Questioning what I believe again. Is faith a decision or something that happens to me? Talked it over with the chaplain for an hour.
The full moon ritual with my friends in the backyard: salt, sage, silence, then wine.
Reading the old texts before bed, one verse at a time. Today's line about letting go hit me hard, especially after the argument with my brother.
Fasted for the holy day and broke the fast with dates and water at sunset, the whole family around the table.
Stood under the stars on the roof and felt very small and very okay about it.
We popped a bottle of cheap prosecco on the fire escape to toast Dani's new job. Fairy lights, paper cups, and way too much cake.
Office potluck for the end of the fiscal year. Someone brought a piñata shaped like a spreadsheet. We all took turns hitting it.
Fireworks over the harbor tonight and the whole street came out with folding chairs. Kids waving sparklers, neighbors sharing lemonade.
Our 10th anniversary dinner. Candles, the good wine, and he'd secretly booked the same corner table from our first date.
Graduation party in the backyard, banner and all. Grandma cried through the whole speech and I did too.
Everybody in the lab crowded around the tiny TV, then the cheering started and somebody got the champagne out of the supply closet.
The whole block turned up with pots and spoons at 8pm when the baby was announced healthy. Noise, hugging, and a conga line down the driveway.
Pulled a long table into the garden, strung up lanterns, and made paella for twenty. Nobody wanted to leave when the sun went down.
Hung streamers in the hallway and baked a lemon cake for the day Mum finished her last round of treatment. Bell rung, kazoos blown. Today felt like a party.
Got engaged!! Dancing in the kitchen at midnight in socks, ring on my finger, phone blowing up with congratulations from everyone.
Diwali night: rows of diyas on the balcony, new clothes, sweets from the shop downstairs, and cousins shouting over the sparklers.
Team won the regional final. Pizza on the bus, singing the whole way home, coach got dunked in the water cooler bucket.
Promoted today. Then drinks with the crew, then karaoke, then a very questionable rendition of a power ballad.
Retirement send-off for Mr. Alvarez after 31 years at the depot. Speeches, a sheet cake with a tiny forklift on it, and a standing ovation.
Found Dad's old cassette tapes in the attic and the smell of the dust and plastic took me straight back to the back seat of the Buick, summer of '94.
I keep thinking about the creek behind our old house, the way we'd flip rocks hunting for crayfish until the streetlights came on.
Flipping through the photo album at my aunt's. There's one of me at six with a missing tooth holding a fish nearly as big as I was.
Heard that song in the grocery store and was instantly sixteen again, driving with the windows down and no destination.
Grandma's kitchen: yellow linoleum, the clock that ticked too loud, her humming while she kneaded dough. I could draw it with my eyes closed.
Remember the blizzard of '08 when school closed for a week and we built a snow fort tall enough to stand in? Went by the old street today and the elm is gone.
Rain on the tin roof. That's all it took. Suddenly I'm eight, at my uncle's farm, shelling peas with a bowl in my lap.
Looked up my college roommate online and spent two hours remembering all the stupid, wonderful things we did in that dorm room.
Our first apartment had a window that wouldn't close and a radiator that clanked all night. I miss it more than I'd have guessed.
Dug out my old Game Boy. The battery compartment was corroded but the cartridge smell was exactly the same. Whole afternoons of my childhood live in that thing.
Walking past the bakery where Papa used to buy us warm rolls every Sunday after church. Same sign, new owners, same smell.
Reread letters from my pen pal in Lisbon from 1999. Her handwriting, the pressed flowers, all of it.
That road trip with Marisol where we got lost in Nevada and ate gas station burritos on the hood of the car. Best week of my twenties.
The funeral reminded me how Uncle Ray used to whistle off-key while fixing things. We all sat swapping stories of him until midnight.

Interview at nine tomorrow. Ironed the blue shirt, printed copies of my resume, and practiced the 'tell me about yourself' bit in the shower.
Three months since the layoff and the savings are thinning. I refresh the job boards before breakfast like it's the news.
They offered me the position! Salary is a bit under what I asked, but benefits are good. Going to ask for a day to think it over.
Take-home assignment due tonight for a design role I'd love. Eight hours in and the layout still looks off to me.
Recruiter ghosted me after saying they'd be in touch 'by Monday.' It's Thursday. I keep checking my inbox anyway.
Started applying to jobs in a different field after ten years in retail. My friend says my customer skills transfer. I hope she's right.
Went to the hiring fair at the convention center and handed out twelve resumes. Feet hurt and I have a free tote bag and one maybe.
Mock interview with my cousin went badly. I rambled for five minutes on one question. Good to find out here instead of there.
Another night of applications, and my partner brought me tea without asking. Told them I'd be done soon and meant it for once.
Priya covered my shift without being asked when she heard about my sick kid. I owe her a lunch at least.
The guy at the next desk chews with his mouth open and taps his pen all day. I've started wearing headphones with no music.
Our team potluck was surprisingly fun. Dave's mystery casserole was actually delicious and we stayed an hour past lunch.
New hire asked me how to set up the printer and then we ended up chatting about hiking for twenty minutes. Nice to have someone new.
Somebody keeps eating the yogurt I label with my name. I'm not saying anything yet but the sticky note might get more aggressive.
Karen from accounting took credit for my spreadsheet in front of the director. I smiled, said nothing, and then fumed in the stairwell.
Birthday card circulating around the office and I wrote something generic. I barely know Tom but he always holds the elevator.
Had a heart to heart with Ahmed at the coffee machine about burnout. Turns out half the floor feels the same.
Lunch with the whole team at the new ramen place. Learned that our quiet analyst is a retired marathon runner. You never know.
The two people on my team who won't speak to each other keep routing everything through me. Feel like a translator at a bad summit.
Marta left a thank-you note on my desk for helping her through the migration. I taped it to my monitor.
Walked into the break room to everyone suddenly going quiet. Maybe it's nothing. It's probably nothing.
Sat in on Jen's first presentation and clapped the loudest. She's been so nervous for weeks and she was great.
Open office is loud, someone's on speakerphone again, and the new guy asked me to 'quickly' look at his code for an hour.
Launched the little Etsy shop tonight. Ten listings, a logo I made myself, and no idea if anyone will find it.
First wholesale order came in, forty candles for a boutique in town. I'm going to need a bigger table.
Spent the morning on invoices and the afternoon on a supplier who sent the wrong boxes. This is not what I imagined 'being my own boss' meant.
Met a possible business partner for lunch. We agree on almost everything except who handles money, which is probably the main thing.
Closed month three with a small profit. Not enough to quit my day job, but it's the first number in black.
Registered the LLC today. The clerk was nice and the receipt is now on my fridge like a diploma.
Customer left a one-star review because the package was late, though that was the courier. Spent an hour drafting a reply.
My bakery stall sold out by ten. Packed up, counted the cash twice, and sat in the van eating the one unsold croissant.
Thinking about hiring a part-time helper for the shop. Can't tell if the busy season is a trend or a fluke.
Dad asked how the landscaping company is going and I gave the honest answer: tired, growing, and not sure about the truck payment.
Spent the weekend building a price sheet and realized I've been undercharging since spring. Raising rates on the first.
Pitched the café idea to my brother over dinner. He asked about margins and I didn't have a number. Homework.
Got my first big client for the consulting work. The contract's three pages and I read every word twice.
Set up a booth at the weekend market, ran out of change by noon. Learned to bring more small bills and a shade umbrella.
Finished day 120 on the Japanese app. I can say 'where is the station' but nobody is going to understand my accent.
Ordered coffee entirely in French today and the barista answered back in French. Didn't switch to English once. Tiny victory.
Flashcards in the bus again. Today's batch is German verbs with separable prefixes and I hate each of them.
Italian class was a disaster. I mixed up 'I'm hot' and 'I'm hungry' in front of the whole group, and the teacher still laughs about it.
Called my grandmother and tried to use the Korean I've been practicing. She cried a little and corrected my grammar at the same time.
Watching Spanish shows with the subtitles in Spanish now, not English. Catching about half of everything. Better than a month ago.
Met my language exchange partner at the library. We traded an hour of Portuguese for an hour of English and both of us left tired.
Stopped looking up every word in the novel and just guessed from context. Slower, but it sticks better.
Mandarin tones still make me feel tone-deaf. My tutor says be patient. I said that's easy for her to say.
Trip to Lisbon next month so I'm cramming restaurant phrases at night. Practicing 'the bill please' on the cat.
Dreamed in Spanish for the first time last night, I think. Couldn't remember what anyone said but it felt real.
Realized I've kept my Duolingo streak for a whole year. The owl is relentless, but I can now read the menu at the Greek place.
Joined a Sunday conversation club. Everyone is nervous and gestures a lot, and nobody cares about mistakes. I love it.
Hearing the neighbors speak Tagalog through the wall and recognizing a few words. I want to knock and say hi in their language.
Made the last payment on the car loan today. Zero. I stared at the screen for a full minute.
Credit card balance is 6,400 and I finally made a spreadsheet to see all of it. Seeing it hurts, but it helps more than not looking.
Student loan statement came in. The number barely moved after two years of payments, and the interest is almost laughable.
Skipped takeout all week to put the extra forty dollars toward the card. It's not much but it's a start.
Collection agency called again. I didn't answer and then felt my chest tighten for an hour afterwards.
We owe my in-laws eight thousand for the down payment and every holiday dinner feels slightly heavy because of it.
Paid off the small card first, the snowball method, and it felt like crossing off a to-do I'd had since 2021.
Called the bank to ask about lowering my interest rate. The rep put me on hold for twenty minutes, then said yes. Why didn't I do this sooner?
Looked at my balance after the vet bill and just closed the laptop. The dog is fine at least.
We're eating beans and rice until March, because the minimum payments are eating us. At least we're on the same page.
Co-signed for my brother years ago and now the payments are landing on me. Not sure how to bring it up without a fight.
Used my tax refund entirely on the balance. Boring, responsible, and honestly one of the better feelings I've had this year.
Medical bills are stacking up after the surgery. Learned there's a payment plan with no interest, so that's a relief.
Cut up the card, finally. Kept the number written down in case I ever feel tempted, which is a little silly.
Twelve weeks today and we finally saw the heartbeat on the ultrasound. I cried in the parking lot before I could even call my mom.
Pregnancy brain is real. Put the milk in the cupboard and my keys in the fridge, and I'm only at week 20.
Felt the baby kick for the first time tonight, just a little flutter under my hand while I was watching TV. Dave put his hand there for ten minutes and felt nothing, which he took personally.
Third trimester and I cannot find a position that works. Pillow wall, three trips to the bathroom, and heartburn that no amount of tums touches.
Took the test again this morning just to be sure. Two lines, still. Haven't told anyone yet, not even Priya, and it's killing me.
Painted the little room pale green this weekend and assembled the crib with the wrong screws twice. Due date is the 3rd and everything suddenly feels very close.
Can't stand the smell of coffee anymore, which is tragic. Crackers by the bed and a nap at 2pm have become my whole personality.
Had to let out the waistband on my work pants again. My coworkers keep asking if I'm hiding something and I just smile.
We chose a name finally. Lena if it's a girl, and I'm not telling the in-laws until the shower so nobody can campaign against it.
Glucose test today, which means I drank the orange stuff and sat in a waiting room for an hour. The midwife says my blood pressure looks great.
Bag is packed by the door, car seat is installed, and my feet look like loaves of bread. Any day now, apparently.
Our baby is due in March and Ahmed already bought a tiny Raptors jersey. I'm just trying to finish the quarterly report before I go on leave.
Two weeks past the due date. Everyone texts 'any news?' and I want to throw my phone into the lake.
Prenatal yoga class was full of women who looked as tired and round as me. Nice to laugh about our ankles together, and I'm sleeping a bit better after.
Second date with Marco tonight. He picked a little Thai place and remembered the thing I'd said about my sister's dog, which got me a bit.
Swiped for an hour and matched with nobody worth answering. Deleting the app again, probably until Thursday.
Setup by my coworker's husband. Blind dinner at 7, I wore the green top, and honestly I'm more nervous than I was before my last job interview.
Three months in and we finally had the 'what are we' talk on the couch. She said she'd been wondering the same thing, and I think I stopped breathing for a second.
He ghosted after two good dates. Not heartbroken, just annoyed that I rearranged my Saturday for it.
Spent forty minutes picking a shirt, changed twice, then he showed up in a hoodie. We ended up walking along the river till it got dark.
Haven't been out with anyone since the divorce, and my friends keep pushing. Agreed to coffee on Sunday with a guy from the book club, so now I'm panicking quietly.
She kissed me goodnight at the bus stop and then got on the 14 without looking back. I'm grinning like an idiot in the rain.
Meeting his parents next weekend. I've already practiced small talk about his dad's tomato plants in the mirror.
We went bowling on the first date and I threw four gutter balls in a row. He still asked for a second one, so maybe the humiliation worked.
Long distance is rough. Video call tonight went an hour and a half and then I stared at the black screen feeling kind of hollow.
Friend dragged me to speed dating at the brewery. Eight conversations, three about sourdough, one actual maybe.
Told Jess I wasn't feeling the spark. Kind about it, I hope, but the car ride home was quiet and my stomach was in knots.
Anniversary is next week and I have no idea what to plan. Maybe the lake cabin, maybe just pizza on the floor like we did when we first moved in.
Had a huge argument with my sister over who gets mom's piano. We both said things in the kitchen that I wish I could take back.
Didn't speak to Rob for two days after the budget meeting blowup. He finally sent a text that said 'lunch?' and I almost cried with relief.
Dishes again. I snapped at Jun about it and the whole evening went sour, and now we're doing the cold-shoulder thing.
Apologized first this time. It cost me a little pride but the tension in the house is gone and we made dinner together.
Dad and I yelled at each other on the phone about politics. We hung up mid-sentence, and I keep replaying it.
Roommate has been leaving passive-aggressive notes on the fridge. I wrote one back, then tore it up and decided to just talk to her tomorrow.
Two of my friends aren't talking and both keep venting to me. I'm tired of being the middle and I'm not sure what to say to either of them.
Heard the whole thing from my manager about the missed deadline and how it was apparently my fault. I stayed calm in the room and then shook in the stairwell.
We finally sat down and hashed it out, no phones, tea going cold. It was awkward and slow but nobody stormed off, which is progress.
Argued with the contractor over the invoice for an hour. He says the tile was extra, I swear it was in the quote.
My brother and I haven't spoken since the wedding last spring. Today I typed a message and deleted it five times.
Words were exchanged in the school pickup line about who cut who off. Embarrassing, honestly, for two adults in minivans.
The group chat turned ugly over a trip itinerary. Someone said 'whatever, do what you want' and now the thread is dead silent.
Teen slammed the door and I let it go for once. We'll talk when we've both cooled off, and I made her favorite soup as an olive branch.
The people upstairs started stomping around at 11 again. Left a polite note on their door about the noise.
Mrs. Alvarez from next door brought over a plate of tamales because she saw me hauling groceries up with a cast on my arm. Best part of my week.
Our neighbor's dog barked from 6am until noon. I'm trying not to be that person but I may need to say something soon.
Block party on Saturday, with a folding table, a cooler of drinks and everyone's kids running around the cul-de-sac. Finally put faces to the names on the mailboxes.
Borrowed a ladder from the guy across the street and returned it with a six-pack. Turns out he grew up two towns over from me.
The fence between our yard and the Hendersons' is leaning again. They offered to split the cost, which was nicer than I expected from the way the last conversation went.
Someone in the building keeps leaving bikes in the hallway and I trip on them every night. Wondering who it is and whether to ask.
Watched the elderly man next door shovel his own driveway at 6am and felt guilty, so I did the rest of it before work. He waved from the window.
New couple moved into the yellow house. I left a loaf of banana bread on their porch with a note, and now I'm wondering if that was weird.
Party next door went past 2am, thumping bass through the wall. I slept with a pillow over my head and I'm useless at work now.
Watered the plants for the family down the hall while they're away. They left a key and a very detailed note about the fern.
Package got delivered to the wrong house again and the guy two doors down walked it over personally. Small mercies.
Argued with the guy next door about where his hedge ends and my lawn starts. Fifteen minutes with a tape measure, and we both sort of laughed at the end.
Our street association meeting turned out to be mostly about a streetlight. I signed the petition, ate a stale cookie and went home.
Went to my cousin Tanya's wedding at the vineyard. The vows were short, the dancing was long, and my feet are wrecked.
Cake tasting this afternoon. We picked lemon with raspberry filling, even though my mom wanted traditional vanilla.
Seating chart is breaking me. Aunt Carol can't sit near uncle Ray and I have exactly one table that doesn't contain a feud.
Wrote a toast for Danny and Lee's wedding on the train. Mostly jokes with one real sentence at the end that made me tear up.
Dress fitting number three. The seamstress pinned the hem and I just stood there looking in the mirror thinking, oh, this is happening.
We put down the deposit on the barn venue today. Seven months out and it already feels real and a little terrifying.
The guest list is at 140 and we said we wanted something small. Cutting second cousins is going to hurt feelings no matter how I do it.
Spent the whole weekend stuffing invitations and licking envelopes. My tongue tastes like glue, but the stack looks lovely.
Rehearsal dinner went well. My dad forgot half his speech and made everyone laugh anyway.
Mailed the RSVP and booked a hotel for Kenji's big day in October. Need a suit that fits, which is a separate adventure.
Our first dance song finally decided: something slow that neither of us can really dance to. Practicing in the kitchen with the lights off.
Bridesmaid group chat has sixty unread messages about shoe colors. I just want to show up and cry at the ceremony.
Got married at city hall on Tuesday with two witnesses and a bakery cupcake. No regrets, only a lot of happy tired.
Flower budget just doubled because apparently peonies are out of season. We're settling on dahlias and I'm okay with it.
Took Mia to the new ramen place on Fifth. The broth was great but we waited forty minutes for a table and she nearly ate her napkin.
Brunch with Mom at the little cafe, with eggs benedict and an overpriced mimosa. She paid, which she always insists on.
Tried the new taco truck by the bus depot. Three tacos for eight dollars and the al pastor was honestly perfect.
Dinner at the Italian place for our anniversary. The server forgot our appetizer and the manager comped dessert, so I can't even be mad.
Too tired to cook, so pizza from the corner place again. That's the third time this week and my wallet knows it.
Lunch with the team at the sushi bar. I had no idea eel could taste like that, I might be converted.
We got seated by the kitchen door and the waiter vanished for twenty minutes. Left a smaller tip than usual and felt weird about it all the way home.
Took the kids to a diner after the soccer game. Pancakes at 4pm and somebody spilled the syrup on the bench, but everyone was happy.
Reservations for 8 and they lost it, so we stood on the sidewalk for an hour. Ended up sharing noodles at a counter and it was the best part.
Late night fries at the diner after the concert, ketchup all over my sleeve and my ears still ringing.
Ordered the spicy Korean fried chicken for lunch and regretted it by 2pm. Totally worth it though.
Solo dinner at the bar of that Mexican place. Nobody to talk to and I didn't mind, just chips and a book.
Our usual Thai spot closed down. Last meal there was a goodbye of sorts, with the owner giving us free mango sticky rice.
Gave in and did the all-you-can-eat buffet with my brother. We ate for two hours and then lay on the couch groaning.
Weekly shop at Aldi, $82 for everything including the good cheese. Forgot the oat milk, of course.
Made a list and actually stuck to it at the store. Only $14 over budget because of the avocados.
Farmers market this morning with peaches, sweet corn and a bag of the weird little carrots. Everything smelled like summer.
Cart was full by aisle three and the cashier said '$163.' I'm not sure how we spend that much on food for two people.
Ran out for milk and came back with chips, salsa, ice cream and no milk. Embarrassing.
Started doing the pickup order so I'm not tempted by the cookie aisle. Someone loaded the bags into my trunk and I felt like a king.
Price of eggs is outrageous again. I stood there for a minute doing math and then bought them anyway.
Heavy bags up three flights, one handle snapped and the oranges rolled down the stairs. A neighbor helped me chase them.
Planned the whole week's dinners on a napkin and then bought only what's on it. Feels like a small act of discipline.
Dragged my toddler through the supermarket and he screamed in the cereal aisle. I bought the cereal just to leave.
Coupons clipped, loyalty card scanned, and I saved six dollars. My grandfather would be proud.
Stocked the fridge for my sister coming to stay, with her favorite yogurt, the weird mustard, and fresh bread. Felt good getting ready for her.
Went hungry to the store, which was a mistake. Basket full of snacks and nothing resembling a meal.
Bought a rotisserie chicken and a bag of salad for dinner and called it a win. Too busy with the move to think harder.
Took four garbage bags of clothes to the donation center. My closet finally closes without a fight.
Finally went through the junk drawer. Found fourteen dead batteries, a passport photo from 2011 and a key to something I can't identify.
Spent Sunday clearing out the garage. Sold the old treadmill online for forty bucks and the whole place feels a size bigger.
Picked up every book I own, kept the ones that made me feel something and boxed the rest. Thirty-two went to the library sale.
Tossed my college notebooks after a long stare. Strange how heavy paper can feel.
Did the kitchen cabinets, expired spices and three mismatched Tupperware lids. I only needed one lid.
My closet has thirty hangers I haven't touched in a year. Took pictures, listed some on resale apps and bagged the rest.
Cleared the kids' toys and let them pick ten to keep. Cried a little, then moved on, and the playroom has a visible floor now.
Dug out my late dad's tools and couldn't make myself throw anything away. Kept the hammer and gave the rest to my cousin.
Every surface in the apartment is clear, and my mind feels clearer too. I might actually enjoy sitting in here tonight.
Looked at the pile of cables in the closet. None of them match anything I own, so they're going to e-waste on Saturday.
Making room before the baby arrives. Three carloads to the thrift store and the spare room is finally empty.
Packed up the apartment and realized I own so much I've never used. Donating half before the movers come.
My mom gave me a box of my childhood drawings and I spent the afternoon deciding what to keep. Photographed most and kept six.
Did the Ridgeline loop with Tomás today, 9 miles and about 2,000 feet of climbing. The last switchback nearly finished me but the view over the reservoir was worth it.
Broke in my new boots on the short trail behind the nature center. No blisters, which is a miracle after last year's disaster.
Trail was muddy from yesterday's rain so we turned around at the creek crossing. Still got to see a pair of deer at the first meadow.
Signed up for the guided sunrise hike at Mount Pell next month. Need to buy a headlamp and figure out how to layer for 30 degrees.
Packed trail mix and way too much water for the Saturday hike with my sister. We counted 14 switchbacks and ate lunch on a rock shaped like a couch.
My calves are screaming on the stairs today. Yesterday we walked up through the pines until the trees got short and the wind got loud, and I stood at the top feeling about nine years old.
Dad insisted on carrying the heavy pack up the mountain even though he's 71. He didn't say much at the summit, just handed me a granola bar and looked out at the valley.
Got to the cairn at the saddle just as the fog lifted. Forty minutes of climbing in my own head and then suddenly the whole range was there.
Found a spot where the path forks and there's a little wooden sign half eaten by moss. Took the left one, ended up at a waterfall nobody was at.
Spent the afternoon walking the ridge with my camera and a thermos. Passed maybe three people all day and I loved every quiet minute.
Got lost for an hour when the blazes disappeared past the old quarry. Phone had one bar and I was honestly a little scared until a woman with two huskies pointed the way back.
Went on a hike with the work crew for the team offsite. Half of them wore sneakers, and our manager got more done in that walk than in two weeks of meetings.
Weekend plan is a trail day with Priya, then laundry and groceries. The knee brace is packed, fingers crossed it holds up.
Twisted my ankle on loose rocks coming down from the overlook. Limped the last two miles and now it's the size of a tangerine.
Finished the first draft of the baby quilt, 36 squares in blue and yellow. The corners don't quite match but she'll never notice.
Spent all of Sunday knitting a scarf for Grandpa. Dropped a stitch around row 40 and had to rip back an hour of work.
Picked up a pottery wheel class at the community center. My first bowl collapsed into a sad little pancake but the teacher said that's normal.
Hot glue gun burned my thumb again while making paper snowflakes for the classroom. The kids loved them anyway.
Cross-stitched the last letter on the nursery sign tonight. Eleven weeks of evenings and it finally says her name.
The shelf by the window is covered in tiny beads, wire, and a half-strung necklace. I told myself I'd tidy up and then sat down for just one more row.
Mom taught me how to crochet a granny square over video call. Mine looks like a lumpy octagon, but she said hers did too at first.
Sewing machine jammed halfway through hemming the curtains. Took out the bobbin case, found a tangled nest of thread, and swore at it for twenty minutes.
Our table at the Saturday market sold out of candles by noon. Counting the cash box, I realized I made more than at my old part-time job.
Made a hand-painted card for my coworker's retirement, with a tiny drawing of her cat. She teared up when she opened it.
Got a bin of fabric scraps at the thrift store for four dollars. Already imagining a patchwork bag with them.
Late-night glue, glitter, and cardboard for my daughter's science fair volcano. It was supposed to be her project but I ended up painting the lava.
Tried to felt a little fox from wool roving and it came out looking like a potato with ears. My partner named it Gerald and now it lives on the desk.
Stayed up later than I should have finishing a macrame plant hanger. Now the fern has a new home and the knots are actually kind of neat.
Binge-listened to the whole series on that missing hiker case on the drive to Denver. Eight episodes and I still don't know who to believe.
New episode of my favorite history show dropped this morning, so my commute was basically a lecture on Byzantine emperors. Loved it.
Started a podcast about personal finance on Marta's recommendation. The hosts are a little smug but I already learned what a Roth IRA is.
Cleaning the whole apartment goes faster with an episode of that true crime comedy show playing. Got through the bathroom and most of a murder.
Recorded my first episode today with my brother on his borrowed microphone. We rambled for 45 minutes about sandwiches and I'm not sure anyone will ever hear it.
Two hosts arguing happily in my ears while I walked the dog. By the time I got home I'd learned how octopus brains work and forgotten to pick up my coffee.
Fell asleep to a guy reading a sleepy story about a lighthouse. Didn't even hear the end, which I guess was the point.
The woman interviewing the beekeeper had such a calm voice that I sat in the parked car for ten extra minutes just to hear how it ended.
Took a long drive to my aunt's house and listened to two strangers talk about space for three hours. I wish I could hang out with them.
Switched my gym playlist for a new Spanish show because someone said it helps the ear. Understood about a third and felt kind of proud.
Weekly episode on mental health from the therapist host hit hard today. I paused it twice and wrote down a few lines.
Subscribed to a show about tiny house building and queued up forty episodes for the long weekend. Meanwhile, I have not finished the actual shelving project in the garage.
Being a guest on a small show about teaching tomorrow. Nervous, but I wrote down three stories to tell in case my mind goes blank.
Cooked a big pot of chili while two comedians told stories about their worst jobs. Laughed so hard I had to turn the stove down.
Got to the concert an hour early and the line already wrapped around the block. Third row, sweaty crowd, and the drummer pointed at me.
Took my nephew to his first baseball game. He cared more about the nachos than the score but did a great wave when the home run happened.
Tickets for the comedy show on Friday are booked. Finally something on the calendar that isn't a meeting.
Went to my cousin's one-act play at the community theater. The lead forgot a line and the whole room held its breath, and then she nailed it.
The street festival downtown had a brass band, face painting, and about nine food trucks. Spent forty dollars on empanadas and don't regret it.
The lights went down and everyone in the arena lifted their phones like tiny stars. I put mine in my pocket and just sang.
Stood in the rain for two hours outside the stadium and nobody left. When the first chord rang out everyone screamed like we'd all been waiting years.
We squeezed into a tiny basement bar where a three-piece band played original songs. The singer apologized for her cold between every one and it was charming.
Arrived at the arena at 6, left at midnight, and my ears are still ringing. I've got a hoarse voice and a sticky souvenir cup.
Sat in the grass with a blanket and watched a symphony play under the stars. My mother leaned her head on my shoulder like when I was little.
Volunteered at the book fair on Saturday, stacking chairs and checking tickets for a lineup of local authors. Got a signed copy and a free sandwich.
Dragged myself to the opening night of the new exhibit at the museum because Dana had an extra pass. I'm glad I did, though my feet will remind me for days.
Bought tickets for the ballgame, parking, and overpriced beer. The team lost by eight but the seventh inning stretch was perfect.
Scored last-minute seats for the touring musical, a work trip bonus for being stuck in the city. The costumes alone were worth the price.
My post about the lemon tree somehow got 400 likes. Replied to a few comments and felt a little bit famous.
Muted three group chats and a handful of accounts that kept making me anxious about the election. The feed is calmer already.
Posted my first video on TikTok, a recipe for dumplings. Eleven views, mostly my cousins.
Old college friend posted engagement photos and I scrolled the whole album twice. Happy for her and also quietly jealous.
Realized I checked my phone fourteen times during dinner. Nobody's even messaging me, I just reach for it like a reflex.
A stranger replied to my story with something mean and I spent an hour drafting a comeback. Then I just blocked them and breathed.
Everyone in my feed seems to have bought a house this year. I know it's a highlight reel, but my rent check still stings.
Got a message from a girl I haven't talked to since eighth grade, and we ended up chatting for an hour about our old teacher.
Screen time report says four hours and twenty minutes a day on my phone. I'm setting a limit on the app and putting it in a drawer after nine.
Spent all morning replying to comments on the shop's page, which is supposed to be marketing but feels like hanging out with customers.
My mom finally figured out how to like a photo. She sent me a thumbs up emoji with seven exclamation marks and I'm keeping the screenshot.
Went viral for a mistake in a work presentation slide and my boss texted me a laughing face. Now I'm triple-checking everything before it goes out.
Trying to take a break from the feed during the weekend. Read a real paper book for two hours instead and my head feels clearer.
Watched the debate with my roommates and we paused it six times to yell at the screen. Nobody changed anybody's mind, but the nachos were great.
Voted early this morning, in and out in ten minutes. The poll worker, a retired teacher, handed me a sticker and said thank you like she meant it.
City council meeting about the new bus route ran until 10 p.m. Fourteen people spoke, and I got two minutes to explain why my street needs a stop.
Called my representative's office about the housing bill. The staffer was kind and took notes, and I felt a little less powerless.
Dinner with Uncle Ray got tense when the election came up. We switched to talking about the Packers and everybody calmed down.
Knocked on forty-three doors today for the school board candidate. Three people were rude, twelve were friendly, and one man gave me a glass of lemonade.
Sat through a long line at the county clerk to register my new address. Got a form, a sticker, and some hope that my vote will count in the primary.
I read the ballot measures twice and still can't tell what a yes vote on Proposition 9 would do. Going to ask my neighbor who follows this stuff.
Cried a little when the results came in. I thought I was done caring about this and apparently I'm not.
Watched the senator's speech on the news and my partner and I argued about taxes the whole way through dinner. We made up over dishes.
Went to a rally downtown with a homemade sign. Marched six blocks chanting and my voice is gone but my heart is full.
Our book club ended up arguing about immigration policy instead of the book. I left feeling raw and a bit sad about it.
Ran into a candidate at the farmers market and shook her hand. She looked tired but asked about my kid's school.
Tried to explain how the electoral college works to my twelve-year-old. She said it sounded made up and honestly she has a point.
Thanksgiving at my in-laws went better than expected. Nobody fought about anything, the turkey was moist, and I took home a whole pie.
Put up the tree this weekend with the kids. The lights were tangled again and my husband swore, but the angel on top looks great.
Easter egg hunt in the backyard with all the cousins. Little Mateo found the golden egg in the first thirty seconds and gloated for an hour.
Fourth of July barbecue at Jen's place. Burgers burned, sparklers lit, and I was asleep by ten with sunburned shoulders.
